MUQATIL:14:18-19/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:18-19/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:18-19/r1.claim: Disbelievers' deeds, done without faith, are like ashes carried off by a fierce wind; they earn no reward and cannot benefit from them.

FARRA:v2p72/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p72/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p72/r4.claim: The likeness is grammatically attributed to the disbelievers, but the simile actually describes their deeds; Arabic can place the intended relation at the end of the phrase.

FARRA:v2p72/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p72/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p72/r5.claim: The genitive reading أعمالهم كرماد is grammatically possible, though the author has not heard it in recitation; poetry illustrates an implied preposition and a fronted noun.

FARRA:v2p73/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p73/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p73/r1.claim: عاصف may describe the day because wind occurs then, just as a day may be called cold or hot; a poem similarly calls days cloudy or sunny.

FARRA:v2p73/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p73/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p73/r2.claim: Alternatively عاصف الريح may omit الريح because it was already mentioned; if عاصف modifies wind alone, it may still take the day's case by proximity.

FARRA:v2p73/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p73/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p73/r3.claim: The cited Arabic examples show case attraction to a neighboring noun, including poetry and the phrase هذا جحر ضب خرب.

FARRA:v2p73/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p73/r4.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
FARRA:v2p73/r4.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab read المتين in the genitive, a reading followed by al-A'mash; the author says nominative is preferable.

FARRA:v2p73/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p73/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p73/r5.claim: The author prefers رفع المتين; the cited poem shows a genitive word attracted to a neighboring noun despite its syntactic role.

MAJAZ:v1p337/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p337/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p337/r5.claim: The comparison means the deeds of the disbelievers are like ash, with deeds understood as the compared object.

MAJAZ:v1p337/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p337/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p337/r6.claim: Qur'an 32:7 means He perfected the creation of everything.

MAJAZ:v1p337/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p337/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p337/r7.claim: Ḥumayd ibn Thawr's line means my piercing reaches you through both sides of the night, illustrating expanded word order.

MAJAZ:v1p337/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p337/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p337/r8.claim: The anonymous line about Hind means her teeth and beauty, rather than Hind herself being the two things.

MAJAZ:v1p339/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p339/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p339/r1.claim: Arabic can assign a container's quality to what it contains: a day is called stormy although the wind within it is what storms.

MAJAZ:v1p339/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p339/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p339/r2.claim: The anonymous verse calls a night sleepless although it is the riding animals that do not sleep.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p232/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p232/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p232/r1.claim: ʿĀṣif means a day of violent wind; the disbelievers' deeds are like ash scattered by wind because God nullifies and obliterates them.

TAB-FULL:v13p622/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r1.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r1.claim: A Basran grammarian supplies an omitted phrase, “among what We recount is the likeness of the disbelievers,” comparing the construction to 13:35.

TAB-FULL:v13p622/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r2.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r2.claim: Kufan grammarians make the deeds the subject of the simile, with the meaning “the deeds of those who disbelieved are like ashes”; they discuss parallel word order and case in 39:60 and 2:217.

TAB-FULL:v13p622/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r3.claim: The verse compares disbelievers’ worldly deeds, which they thought were for God, to ash blown away; their mixed idolatrous works cannot benefit them at Judgment because they were not done purely for God.

TAB-FULL:v13p622/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r4.claim: The far-off error is the disbelievers’ deeds: they were done without guidance or sound direction, far from the straight path.

TAB-FULL:v13p622/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p622/r5.claim: عاصف is grammatically attached to “day,” describing it by the wind that occurs in it, like calling a day hot or cold.

TAB-FULL:v13p623/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p623/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p623/r1.claim: The wording may mean “on a stormy-wind day,” with الريح omitted because it was already mentioned; poetry likewise omits a noun after يوم.

TAB-FULL:v13p623/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p623/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p623/r2.claim: Alternatively, عاصف describes الريح but follows the case of the nearby word يوم; Arabic poetry and the phrase “a ruined lizard’s burrow” show case attraction.

TAB-FULL:v13p623/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p623/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v13p623/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the wind carried the ashes on the stormy day.

TAB-FULL:v13p623/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p623/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p623/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says those who worshiped other than God find none of their deeds useful at Judgment, just as wind makes ashes uncontrollable.

ZAJJAJ:v3p157/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p157/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p157/r1.claim: The clause ‘the likeness of those who disbelieve’ may be an elliptical topic, a phrase understood from the recitation, or an adjective describing those whose deeds are like ashes.

ZAJJAJ:v3p157/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p157/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p157/r2.claim: The meaning is that everything disbelievers offer to draw near to God is rendered worthless, as other verses say their deeds are annulled or lost.

NAHHAS:v2p365/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p365/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p365/r3.claim: Al-Kisa'i parses works as the comparison; Abu Ja'far rejects dialectal مثل جحر ضب خرب as Qur'anic grammar and parses عاصف by ellipsis.

THALABI:v5p311/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p311/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p311/r1.claim: The verse likens unbelievers' deeds to ash scattered by storm winds: what they earned gives them nothing, and this is far-reaching loss.

THALABI:v5p311/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p311/r2.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v5p311/r2.claim: Al-Farra explains the syntax by attaching the likeness to the unbelievers while making their deeds the predicate, following Arabic word order that places the familiar subject first.

THALABI:v5p311/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p311/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p311/r3.claim: The source compares the construction with verses where the order means God made every thing's creation beautiful and where the faces of those who lied against God are darkened.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r1.claim: The deeds of disbelievers are like useless ash, the remaining trace of burned matter; a violent gale scatters it beyond recovery, just as disbelief leaves their deeds without benefit.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r3.claim: In في يوم عاصف, the day is described as stormy because the wind occurs on that day, like calling a day cold or hot.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, في يوم عاصف means a day of stormy wind, with الريح omitted because wind was already mentioned.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r5.claim: A third grammatical explanation keeps عاصف as an adjective of the previously mentioned wind, but its later position makes it follow the case of اليوم.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r6.claim: They cannot obtain any reward in the afterlife for their good works in this world because disbelief nullified those works.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, they cannot benefit in the afterlife from worldly possessions acquired through their sins.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128#2/r8.claim: Their error is called far-reaching because death makes it impossible to repair or compensate for it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p439/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p439/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p439/r1.claim: He parses the nominative parable as introducing what is being recited to the audience, a construction also held by Sibawayh.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p439/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p439/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p439/r2.claim: He supplies the omitted noun deeds: the deeds of those who disbelieve are like ashes. Arabic can place the more definite genitive first and state the described noun afterward.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p439/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p439/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p439/r3.claim: The commentary refers to its fuller discussion of the several analyses under the parable of the Garden promised to the God-fearing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r1.claim: He defines ashes as the fine particles of burned charcoal, reduced to extremely fine dust.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r2.claim: The verb rāmada is also used of placing meat in ashes, as in the proverb about roasting meat and then putting it in ashes.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r3.claim: They explain ʿāṣif as a wind that blows strongly.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r4.claim: He says the adjective follows the grammatical case of day although it describes wind: a day may be called cold or hot because those conditions occur in it; Abu Ubayda cites a night described as sleeping for the same reason.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r5.speaker: أبو حاتم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r5.claim: He treats this as ordinary Arabic attribution, comparing the night and day being assigned actions or qualities that belong to what occurs in them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r6.claim: His other parse supplies wind: a day fierce with wind, with the noun omitted because wind was mentioned earlier; he cites a poem that similarly omits sun after mentioning it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r7.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r7.claim: They explain the parable as the unbelievers' acts offered to God being null and useless because they associated others with Him, like ash scattered by wind.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p440/r8.claim: He says the unbelievers will find no reward in the afterlife for what they did in this world.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p443/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p443/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p443/r1.claim: He glosses distant error as great loss: their deeds vanish like ashes, and the loss is distant from any hope of return.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p443/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p443/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p443/r2.claim: He glosses it as prolonged error, meaning the unbelievers' way is far from guidance and return.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r5.claim: The deeds of disbelievers resemble ash scattered by a fierce wind; any deeds they offer are null and useless because they associated others with God.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r6.claim: They will find no reward for their deeds; their work's disappearance is the great loss and distant misguidance.

JISHUMI:v5p3849/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī read خالق as an active participle and put the following nouns in genitive; the others read خلق as a past verb with the nouns as its objects.

JISHUMI:v5p3849/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r3.claim: Shadd denotes running; ishtidād is accelerated movement with strength, as when pain intensifies quickly.

JISHUMI:v5p3849/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r4.claim: Wind is moving air, and ʿāṣif describes strong wind.

JISHUMI:v5p3849/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r6.speaker: سيبويه والبصرية
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r6.claim: They analyze the nominative mathal as a fronted clause meaning ‘what is recited or narrated to you is an example,’ with أعمالهم كرماد as its predicate.

JISHUMI:v5p3849/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r7.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r7.claim: He analyzes it as ‘the example of the works of those who disbelieved’; Arabs may introduce the known noun before its predicate, as in 22:19.

JISHUMI:v5p3849/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v5p3849/r8.claim: A third analysis makes mathal an extra connective, so the meaning is simply that the disbelievers' deeds are like ashes.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r1.claim: The comparison concerns the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord, like the phrasing about faces of those who lied about God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r2.claim: Calling the day stormy describes the wind present in it, just as a day may be called hot or cold for what it contains.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r3.claim: Another explanation supplies an omitted word: a day of stormy wind, since wind was already mentioned.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342#2/r4.claim: God's parable says unbelievers gain no benefit from worldly deeds because they associated others with God, like ash scattered by wind.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p343/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p343/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p343/r1.claim: In the afterlife, unbelievers cannot obtain anything from what they earned in worldly life; this is utter misguidance.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r1.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r1.claim: Sibawayh supplies an introductory phrase such as what is recited or told to you before مثل الذين كفروا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r2.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r2.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and al-Farra make مثل the subject and كرماد its predicate, with the sense that the unbelievers’ works are like ash.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r3.claim: Al-Farra also reportedly allows مثل to be redundant, yielding the direct sense that the unbelievers’ works are ash.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r4.claim: The author prefers treating مثل and أعمالهم as successive subjects, with the whole sentence Works are like ash as the predicate of the first.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r5.claim: The works of unbelievers vanish when needed like ash blown away by fierce wind, leaving no trace or recoverable gain.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r6.claim: The day is called ʿāṣif though the wind is literally what blows fiercely; the description extends from wind to the day in which it occurs.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r7.claim: Nafiʿ and Abu Jaʿfar read الرياح in the plural; the other readers use the singular الريح.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r8.claim: That points to the unbelievers’ condition and their deep misguidance, far from the clear road to salvation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331#2/r9.claim: Al-Sulami reads يوم عاصف in an annexed construction; he also reports a reading of ألم تر with a silent rāʾ meaning do you not know.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r10.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:14:17-18/r10.claim: The comparison means the works of those who disbelieve; the construct phrase omits ‘works’ before ‘those who disbelieve’ because it is repeated afterward.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r11.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:14:17-18/r11.claim: Alternatively, it means the likeness of the unbelievers themselves among what has been related about them.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:17-18/r12.claim: Their deeds yield little benefit: like ashes scattered by a violent wind, they cannot be gathered or used; this parallels the verse about works made scattered dust.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:17-18/r13.claim: The far misguidance is the deeds’ remoteness from benefit.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:14:17-18/r14.claim: Alternatively, it is error far removed from what is right.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:17-18/r15.claim: The verse refutes determinism because it attributes the deeds to the unbelievers; if God created those deeds, attributing them to the people would be invalid.

TABRISI:14:17/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:17/r2.claim: مثل الذين كفروا is estimated as 'the likeness of those who disbelieved in their Lord' or treated as an inserted word; their deeds are a genitive-like appositional subject and 'ashes' is the predicate.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r1.claim: Al-Farra says the likeness is grammatically attributed to the disbelievers, though the actual comparison is to their deeds; he compares another verse.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r2.claim: Calling the day “windy” though the wind is what blows is permissible because the day's weather is described by the wind, like a hot or cold day.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, “wind” is omitted after it was already mentioned, as in a cited line about a day whose sun is obscured.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh supplies an omitted introduction: “among what We recount to you is the likeness of the disbelievers,” then begins “their deeds are like ashes.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r5.speaker: النخعي وابن يعمر والجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r5.claim: These readers omit tanwīn on yawm in “in a windy day.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r6.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r6.claim: The commentators say all deeds by which polytheists seek nearness are null and useless, like ashes scattered by the wind; they find no reward in the afterlife.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354#2/r7.claim: “That is distant misguidance” means being far from salvation.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r1.claim: A second view identifies the deeds as idol worship and disbelief that they mistakenly thought was faith and a path to salvation; their labor becomes a burden.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r2.claim: A third view includes both categories: their real good works and their supposed good works are void, deepening their regret and constituting distant error.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r3.claim: A variant reads الرياح, plural winds; the adjective عاصف grammatically modifies the day for the wind in it, like a rainy day, or means a day of strong winds with الريح omitted; another reading uses genitive.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra allows interpreting the wording as a day of violent winds or a day whose wind is violent, with wind omitted because it was already mentioned.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r5.claim: They can draw no useful benefit from what they earned in this world or the next because it has been wholly spoiled.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p83#2/r6.claim: The verse supports the view that human beings acquire their actions.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r1.claim: After describing their punishment, God says all the disbelievers' deeds become void and useless; they will find only punishment and their worldly work will leave no trace, the height of loss.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r2.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r2.claim: Sibawayh supplies an omitted frame for the nominative mathal: their example is in what is recited to you; their deeds as ash then answers a tacit question.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r3.claim: Al-Farra parses the phrase as the likeness of the deeds of those who disbelieve, with أعمالهم supplying an omitted genitive noun, as in Q 32:7 and Q 39:60.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r4.claim: Other grammatical analyses make the phrase mean the description of the disbelievers is that their deeds are ash, make أعمالهم an appositive to مثل, or treat مثل as an extra particle.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r5.claim: The simile is that a violent wind scatters ash until it leaves no trace, just as disbelief nullifies deeds completely.

RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p83/r6.claim: One view identifies the nullified works as good deeds such as charity, maintaining family ties, honoring parents, and feeding the hungry; disbelief cancels their benefit.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r1.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r1.claim: Sībawayh parses mathalu as a subject with an omitted predicate, then restarts with their deeds are like ashes; the comparison means like a heap of ashes.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r10.speaker: ابن أبي إسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r10.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Bakr read fī yawmin ʿāṣif with the variant recorded here.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r11.claim: They means the unbelievers; in the afterlife they gain no reward from their worldly good deeds because disbelief nullified them, a loss made irrecoverable by death.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj supplies the sense: the example of the disbelievers in what is recited to you is their deeds, like ashes.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r3.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows deleting mathal so the sense is that those who disbelieve have deeds like ashes; he also offers an omitted genitive, like the deeds of those who disbelieve.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r4.claim: Another parse makes mathal a predicate-like subject meaning description, or makes aʿmālahum a genitive apposition of inclusion to alladhīna.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r5.claim: The passage connects to 14:15: the deeds of unbelievers are null and unaccepted because they associated others with God.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r6.claim: Ashes are what remains after burning; God likens unbelievers' deeds to ashes erased by a fierce wind on a stormy day, because their deeds involved associationism.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r7.claim: The day may be called stormy because wind occurs during it, as hot and cold days are named for their weather; alternatively day ʿāṣif can mean a day with wind, with the referenced wind omitted.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r8.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r8.claim: Al-Harawī gives the first two explanations of the day being described as stormy, including the poetic ellipsis in which a dark sun is called eclipsed.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r9.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:14:18-20/r9.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī and al-Māwardī give a third parse: ʿāṣif describes the wind, but follows the grammatical case of the preceding word day, like a lizard's ruined hole.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r1.claim: The opening simile can be an omitted predicate about the disbelievers' strange likeness, with their deeds as the explanation, or their deeds may themselves be the subject and ashes the predicate.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r2.speaker: نافع
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r2.claim: Nafi reads الرياح in the plural.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r3.claim: A stormy day describes the time hyperbolically, as in saying the day fasts and the night stands in prayer.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r4.claim: Their charities, kinship, aid to the distressed, manumission, and other virtues vanish because they lacked knowledge of God and orientation toward Him.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r5.claim: Alternatively, their deeds are idol worship, like ashes scattered by a violent wind.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:18/r6.claim: On Judgment Day they find no reward or trace from what they earned; this summarizes the simile and their far-reaching error despite thinking themselves good.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r1.claim: The opening likeness has an omitted predicate, 'the likeness of those who disbelieved'; likeness here is a metaphor for an extraordinary quality.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r2.claim: Their good deeds, including kinship, freeing slaves, ransoming captives, and hosting guests, are ashes blown away because they rest on no foundation of faith.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r3.speaker: المدني
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r3.claim: The Madinan reading has the plural 'winds' where the other reading has 'wind.'

NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r4.claim: The ash image means they will find no trace or reward from their deeds, just as scattered ash cannot be recovered.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p227/r5.claim: The final phrase points to how far their error is from the right path or from reward.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r1.speaker: ابن عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r1.claim: He defines ash as matter pulverized by burning into dust, gives the plural forms r-m-d and armida, notes the rare armidāʾ, and says ramād ramadd is the finest, lightest dust.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r10.claim: Mathal is metaphorical for an unusual quality; ‘their deeds are like ash’ is a resumed answer to an implied question about their likeness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r11.claim: He reports the Kisaʾī and al-Farrāʾ analysis that mathal is suspended, yielding ‘those who disbelieved: their deeds are like ash.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r12.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r12.claim: He makes mathal the subject, aʿmāluhum an encompassing بدل, and ka-ramād the predicate, citing a poetic construction as a parallel.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r2.claim: Jazaʿ is inability to endure hardship, the opposite of patience; a poem illustrates the word mujzaʿan.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p421/r9.claim: The phrase begins with mathal as a subject whose predicate is omitted, estimated as ‘in what is recited to you’ or ‘is being told,’ following Sībawayh.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r1.claim: He offers deeds as a بدل of ‘the likeness of those who disbelieve,’ with an implied ‘the likeness of their deeds,’ and ka-ramād as predicate.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān refers readers to the explanation of ʿaṣf in Yūnus, at the phrase ‘a raging wind struck it.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r11.claim: On allowing a noun to be annexed to its adjective, the reading can mean that on Judgment Day disbelievers find no reward or trace from their works, like scattered ash.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r12.claim: Another explanation supplies an omitted word: they cannot obtain any reward from what they earned.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r2.claim: He prefers treating mathal and aʿmāluhum as successive subjects, with ‘like ash’ predicating the latter and the whole clause predicating the former; their deeds vanish when needed like wind-scattered ash.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the analysis Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers: the clause lacks a link to mathal and is not identical in meaning to it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r4.claim: The disbelievers' seemingly good deeds—kinship, freeing captives, hospitality, helping the distressed, and protection—come to nothing because they lacked knowledge of God, faith, and action for Him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r5.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r5.claim: They read al-rīyāḥ in the plural; most readers read al-rīḥ in the singular.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r6.claim: Calling the day stormy transfers an adjective of wind to the day by figurative usage, as in expressions such as a day that is sun-dark and sun-eclipsed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r7.speaker: الهروي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r7.claim: He supplies ‘wind’ after ‘stormy day,’ deleted because wind was already mentioned; a poem likewise means a day whose sun is dark and eclipsed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r8.claim: Another grammatical explanation makes ʿāṣif an adjective of wind placed after day and genitive by attraction, as in ‘a lizard hole that is ruined.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r9.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وإبراهيم بن أبي بكر عن الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p422/r9.claim: They read ‘in a day of storm,’ construing the adjective as standing for an omitted noun: a day of a violent wind.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r1.claim: رماد is fire-pulverized matter; plural forms include رمد, أرمدة, and rare أرمداء.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r10.claim: عاصف and معصف come from العصف, broken crop stalks, describing a wind that breaks what it passes.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r2.claim: رماد can mean a year of drought; أرمد الماء means it became ash-colored, and الأرمد is gray.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r3.claim: رمد can mean mosquito because of its color; رماد رمدد means reduced to dust.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r4.claim: اشتدت به الريح is an adjective of رماد, and في يوم attaches to اشتدت.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r5.claim: عاصف may stand for عاصف ريحه; الريح is omitted and the day is figuratively described as windy; al-Harawi cites poetry for a similar omission.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r6.speaker: الهروي
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r6.claim: Al-Harawi explains the omission because الريح was mentioned earlier, comparing كاسف for كاسف الشمس in a poem.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r7.claim: Alternatively عاصف is a relational adjective: a day possessing violent wind, like laban and tamir.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r8.claim: A proposed genitive of proximity is rejected: unlike جحر ضب خرب, عاصف cannot properly modify الريح here because definiteness differs.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r9.speaker: الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#2/r9.claim: They read يوم عاصف in an إضافة, with ريح understood, or an adjective added to its noun per that grammatical view.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#3/r1.claim: لا يقدرون is independent; making it modify يوم with omitted فيه is weak.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18#3/r2.claim: مما كسبوا attaches to an omitted phrase as a circumstantial modifier of شيء; after شيء it would be adjectival.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r1.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r1.claim: Sibawayh makes مثل a subject with omitted predicate “the likeness of disbelievers [in what is recited]”; أعمالهم كرماد answers an implied question.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers مثل as subject, أعمالهم as a second subject, and كرماد as its predicate; the author defends the lack of a separate link because the likeness and works are the same.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r3.claim: The Shaikh objects that this predicate has no رابط to مثل; the author compares the identity to هجيرى أبي لا إله إلا الله.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r4.claim: Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra treat مثل as extra, yielding “the works of those who disbelieve are like ashes”; the author rejects extra nouns.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes أعمالهم a بدل کل from مثل, with an omitted إضافة: مثل أعمالهم.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r6.claim: Another parse makes أعمالهم بدل اشتمال, exemplified by al-Zabba's line about camels and their gait.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r7.claim: A further parse makes أعمالهم the predicate of مثل, understood as مثل أعمالهم, while كرماد predicates an omitted subject.

SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:14:18/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa notes a hypothetical غير-transmitted reading with أعمالهم as a genitive بدل اشتمال from الذين.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486#2/r1.claim: The verse compares the deeds of disbelievers who worship others with God and deny His messengers to ash on an unstable foundation: their works collapse when they most need them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486#2/r2.claim: At the Resurrection they seek reward for deeds they thought worthwhile but find nothing, just as storm winds scatter ash beyond their ability to gather it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486#2/r3.claim: Their distant misguidance is working without a sound basis or upright direction and thereby losing the reward they desperately need.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r6.claim: The disbelievers’ good deeds are like ash scattered by a violent wind: charity, freeing slaves, and ransoming captives yield them nothing at Judgment because the deeds lack a foundation.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r7.claim: The parable also evokes a traveler whose route misleads him into remote ravines where he cannot remain or return, so he perishes lost.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya, with al-Ḥawfī, allows a second parsing in which “their deeds” is a new subject whose predicate also completes the first clause.

DURR-FULL:v5p16/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the disbelievers worshipped other than God; their deeds on Judgment Day are like storm-blown ash, useless to them as scattered ash cannot be grasped.

DURR-FULL:v5p16/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r8.speaker: السدي وابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says the wind leaves no trace of the disbelievers' deeds, while Ibn Jurayj glosses the wind's action as carrying the ash away.

BURSEVI:v4p270/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p270/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p270/r1.claim: The parable’s syntax may make the disbelievers’ strange condition the subject and their deeds like ashes its predicate, or leave the predicate implicit and explain it in a new sentence.

BURSEVI:v4p270/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p270/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p270/r2.claim: The wind’s ‘intensifying’ means rushing away with the ashes; the day is called stormy by metonymy for its strong wind.

BURSEVI:v4p270/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p270/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p270/r3.claim: At resurrection the disbelievers find no reward or mitigation in their good deeds, just as no trace remains of ash scattered by a gale.

BURSEVI:v4p270/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p270/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p270/r4.claim: Their compounded error is disbelief, ostentation, and pride in deeds they imagine good; unlike sinful believers, they do not repent because they see no fault in themselves.

BURSEVI:v4p270/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p270/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p270/r5.claim: Charity, kinship, freeing slaves or captives, helping the distressed, and hospitality are nullified when done without knowledge of God, faith, and seeking His face, like ashes blown away.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r1.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r1.claim: Sibawayh treats مثل الذين كفروا as a subject with an omitted predicate, meaning their remarkable description is what is recited here.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r10.claim: The deeds may be noble social acts such as kinship, manumission, freeing captives, hospitality, and aid to the distressed; they may also be sacrifices to idols, and the broader reading may include both.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r11.claim: The clause that their deeds are ashes answers why they ended in ruin by explaining the likeness under discussion.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya instead makes مثل الذين كفروا the subject and أعمالهم كرماد its predicate.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r3.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r3.claim: Al-Hawfi objects that the predicative clause lacks a link back to the subject and is not identical with it in meaning.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r4.speaker: السمين
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r4.claim: Al-Samin answers that the clause can itself name what is said of them, so no linking pronoun is needed; this makes مثل mean their description.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r5.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r5.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and al-Farraʾ treat مثل as an inserted element placed before or after the noun it accompanies.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r6.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r6.claim: Al-Hawfi also parses مثل as subject, كرماد as predicate, and أعمالهم as an appositive of inclusion.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows أعمالهم to replace مثل الذين كفروا if an omitted مثل أعمالهم is supplied, magnifying the comparison.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r8.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r8.claim: Al-Kashf calls the proposed apposition total because the likeness of the disbelievers and likeness of their deeds coincide in essence; another analysis calls it inclusion because the relations differ.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r9.speaker: ابن عيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿIsa defines ashes as a body pulverized by burning into dust and notes its plural forms.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r1.claim: The cited poetic line shows an adjective phrase describing a day darkened by the sun, supporting an analysis that supplies an omitted noun; al-Alusi calls that analysis weak.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r2.claim: Making عاصف an adjective of الريح by grammatical attraction fails because the words differ in definiteness; the plural reading الرياح makes that account even less plausible.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r3.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وإبراهيم بن أبي بكر عن الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r3.claim: They read في يوم عاصف with genitive عاصف; Abu Hayyan explains it by omitting يوم's described noun, while another permits direct annexation of noun and adjective.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r4.claim: The disbelievers cannot obtain any effect of reward or relief from their worldly deeds on Judgment Day; the alternative supplies an omitted word for reward, but the direct reading is stronger.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r5.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r5.claim: Aisha asks whether Ibn Judʿan benefits from feeding the poor and keeping kinship ties in pagan times; the Prophet says it does not benefit him because he lacked faith and repentance for Judgment Day.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r6.claim: The ashes image depicts deeds rendered futile and dispersed because they lacked belief, knowledge of God, and devotion to Him; it also mocks idolaters' belief that idols intercede.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p204/r7.claim: ذلك refers to the evident misguidance of people who assumed they had achieved something; their error is far from truth and right guidance.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r1.claim: The parable explains why the charitable and hospitable good works of unbelievers bring them no benefit in the afterlife, answering the question raised by their severe punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r2.claim: المثل means an extraordinary condition; the intended comparison is the condition of their deeds, expressed through an elliptical nominal construction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r3.claim: Their many accumulated deeds resemble a heap of ash scattered by strong wind: a large collection vanishes so completely that it cannot be reassembled.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r4.claim: Describing the day as stormy is a rational metaphor for its wind being stormy, like calling it a rainy day; compare Q 10:22.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p212#2/r5.claim: The ash image subtly evokes hospitality, one of the unbelievers' best-known virtues: abundant ash from cooking became an idiom for generosity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p213/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p213/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p213/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Jaʿfar read اشتدت به الرياح in the plural; the other readers have singular الريح, with no difference in meaning because the definite noun denotes a genus.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p213/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p213/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p213/r2.claim: The statement that they cannot benefit from what they earned explains the parable: their deeds are futile in the afterlife.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p213/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p213/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p213/r3.claim: “That is distant misguidance” summarizes their state; distant means the utmost degree of misguidance, as in Q 4:116.

TABATABAI:14:15-18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:15-18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:15-18/r7.claim: The violent-wind image likens unbelievers’ deeds to ashes blown away, leaving them no result that can bring happiness; the verse concludes the preceding speech as its outcome.

TABATABAI:14:6-18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:6-18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:6-18/r1.claim: The deeds of unbelievers are like ash scattered by a fierce wind, with no trace remaining, as in the image of deeds made scattered dust; no omitted word such as deeds needs to be supplied, and the verse is a conclusion rather than Moses’s continued speech.

ASAD-NOTES:14:18#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:18#n24/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:14:18#n24/r1.claim: Razi says the works compared to ashes include even good deeds.

ASAD-NOTES:14:18#n25/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:18#n25/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:18#n25/r1.claim: The definite article intensifies the extreme degree of straying; the phrase occurs only here and at 22:12, referring in both to denial of God's oneness and uniqueness.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Verses 18–22 depict disbelievers' efforts vanishing, followed by leaders, followers, and Satan disowning and cursing one another.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: In the afterlife, disbelieving leaders and followers curse one another, and Satan disowns his followers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The addressed disbelievers are polytheists; polytheism is disbelief, and only monotheistic belief is acceptable.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Associating others with God in His being, attributes, or rights is unacceptable and amounts to denying Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The ashes image concerns the polytheists’ deeds on Judgement Day, deeds they had regarded as virtuous.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The deviation is an error from which they cannot return; a profound parallel appears in the cited verses.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:18/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:18/r1.claim: The verse answers whether worldly good works by disbelievers, such as helping the poor and hosting guests, benefit them in the afterlife: however good or numerous, without faith they are like windblown ash, rewarded in this world but useless in the next.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:18/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:18/r2.claim: Faith in God and His messengers is the prior obligation; disbelievers’ socially beneficial works remain valuable to people but bring no afterlife benefit when done without belief in God and the Hereafter.

QIRAAT-ER:14:18:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:18:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:14:18:11#1/r1.claim: The plural winds reading may diffuse or multiply destructive force, challenging the usual association of singular winds with punishment and plural winds with mercy.

STUDYQURAN:14:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r1.claim: As ashes vanish in a storm, disbelievers' deeds are nullified because of their disbelief, leaving no trace.

STUDYQURAN:14:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r2.claim: One interpretation is that the deeds are good actions, such as charity and feeding the hungry.

STUDYQURAN:14:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that the deeds are evil actions, such as idol worship.

STUDYQURAN:14:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r4.claim: A third interpretation is that the deeds combine good and bad actions.

STUDYQURAN:14:18/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r5.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r5.claim: On Judgment Day, disbelievers receive no trace of heavenly reward for what they did.

STUDYQURAN:14:18/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r6.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r6.claim: This means they will not benefit even from their good deeds.

STUDYQURAN:14:18/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r7.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r7.claim: Extreme error means the farthest distance from the path of Truth.

STUDYQURAN:14:18/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r8.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r8.claim: Extreme error can also mean the profound grief and regret at realizing one's deeds were wasted.

STUDYQURAN:14:18/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:18/r9.claim: The Quran elsewhere describes the deeds of disbelievers as brought to naught.

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r10.claim: Ingratitude for God’s many blessings typifies those who lose in the Hereafter.
